findings.passage: So, with what’s going on in our nation today, with the controversy in Georgia, Arizona, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Wisconsin, talk a little bit about Tennessee, the fact that we have photo ID, we don’t have same-day registration, we have the ability for you to request a ballot. So, speak to that just a little bit because there is a misconception between a mail-in ballot and an absentee ballot.
findings.note: As host of his own podcast, he asks the Secretary of State about Tennessee's photo ID requirement, no same-day registration and the ability to request a ballot, and about the difference between mail-in and absentee ballots. A question, not a stated position.
subjects: voter ID at the polls
mail-ballot ID

provenance.fetched_by: source-collector

findings.passage: —because this is something that has come up in the last several weeks is the fact that—how often do we purge our voter rolls in the state of Tennessee? Because that has been a controversy in some of the states that they’re mailing ballots to individuals that are deceased; they’re mailing ballots to individuals that have not lived at an address for 12 months or longer. So, how does Tennessee go about purging its voter rolls to make sure that we are allowing that person that is duly registered that lives at that address to come in and vote and we try to mitigate any kind of voter fraud?
findings.note: In the same podcast he asks how Tennessee purges its voter rolls so that duly registered residents can vote while voter fraud is mitigated. A question, not a stated position.
subjects: voter-roll checks
election integrity laws in general
